bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Devops Engineer Salary

Whether you are negotiating a new role or reviewing an offer, knowing how to convert an hourly rate to an annual salary is essential. This guide uses the latest Fair Work Commission and Australian Bureau of Statistics data to help you estimate your devops engineer salary, including tax, Medicare levy, and superannuation.

### The National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the national minimum wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1004.90 per week for 38 ordinary hours. This is the legal floor for award-free employees. Many devops engineers are covered by an enterprise agreement or a modern award such as the Professional Employees Award. If you are award-covered, your minimum rate will be higher. Check the [pay guides](/blog) for your specific classification. Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the minimum rate, bringing the casual national minimum wage to $33.05 per hour.

### Converting Hourly to Annual: The Formula

The standard calculation is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, this simplifies to hourly rate × 1976. For example, if your hourly rate is $54.83 (the approximate full-time adult average weekly earnings from the ABS), your annual salary is:

$54.83 × 38 × 52 = $108,400 (rounded)

This figure assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, and no allowances. It is a starting point for budgeting and comparison.

### Fortnightly and Weekly Pay

Your weekly pay is your hourly rate multiplied by your weekly hours. For the example above, weekly pay is $54.83 × 38 = $2083.54. Fortnightly pay is double that: $4167.08. Many employers pay fortnightly, so this is a useful figure for cash flow planning.

### Tax and Medicare Levy

Your annual gross pay is subject to income tax and the Medicare levy. For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income between $18,201 and $45,000
- 30% on income between $45,001 and $135,000
- 37% on income between $135,001 and $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

The Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. For a devops engineer earning $108,400, the estimated tax is approximately $24,667 and Medicare levy $2,168, leaving a take-home pay of about $81,565 per year. Use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator for your exact figures.

### Superannuation: Paid on Top

Your employer must pay superannuation guarantee contributions of 12% of your ordinary earnings, on top of your salary. This is not deducted from your pay. For the example above, super is $108,400 × 12% = $13,008 per year. The super guarantee is capped at the maximum contribution base of $270,830. If your earnings exceed that, super stops at the cap. Learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Casual Loading and Other Considerations

If you are a casual employee, your hourly rate includes a 25% loading. When using the [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool, do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading. Instead, enter your base rate and check the casual loading box. The tool will add 25% on top. For award-covered employees, penalty rates and allowances may apply. Refer to the [reference tables](/data) for your award.

### Comparing Your Devops Engineer Salary

The ABS Average Weekly Earnings for full-time adult ordinary time employees is $2083.70 per week (May 2026), which equates to $54.83 per hour. This is a useful benchmark for a devops engineer salary, though actual rates vary by experience, location, and industry. For the most accurate comparison, consult the [job pay](/topics/job-pay) resources or your industry award.

### Summary

To estimate your annual devops engineer salary:

1. Identify your hourly rate (base, excluding casual loading).
2. Multiply by 38 (hours per week) and then by 52 (weeks per year).
3. Add 12% super on top (if applicable).
4. Subtract estimated tax and Medicare levy to find take-home pay.

Remember that this is an estimate. Your actual pay may differ due to overtime, allowances, salary sacrifice, or enterprise agreements. Always check your pay slip and consult the [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page for the latest rates.
